article.name: Aukora Kernel

contact.note: Published in the official security policy.

article.summary: Aukora Kernel is an authority-and-receipt framework, not a standalone memory database. At the reviewed repository head, memory behavior sits in broader Symbiote host/reference layers: a local IDE JSONL store and an internal Convex memory path. The portable @aukora/kernel verifier/reducer has no persistence capability. This review records source observations only; no runtime or benchmark results were produced.

who_what.text: The official repository belongs to the aumara-xyz organization and presents Aukora as an authorization-and-receipt framework for agents. Its README distinguishes a portable verifier/reducer from the broader PROVEN-LAB reference application; the reviewed memory implementations are in Symbiote host/reference layers.

architecture.text: The portable packages/kernel boundary is a deterministic verifier/reducer with no filesystem, network, Convex, or persistence capability. Memory behavior therefore belongs to surrounding host/reference code and should not be attributed to the portable package itself.

The local IDE path stores JSONL entries and a separate JSONL receipt log. Entry payloads carry actor, chainKey, sequence, remember/forget operation, tier, content hash and timestamp; entries also carry a previous hash, nullable content and lifecycle status. The separate receipts carry authorization-argument and content hashes rather than plaintext.

The Convex path stores owner-root and writer identity, delegation ID, receipt and content hashes, source node, visibility, key/value and optional embedding on aukora_memory rows. The reviewed schema and implementation use owner/key and owner indexes, a search index and a vector index.

behavior.text: Local remember sends the content through the shared memory permission gate, hashes the content, appends and fsyncs a receipt first, then rewrites and fsyncs the entry file. A failure returns a fail-closed pause result. The module labels recall advisory-only and does not let stored text authorize effects.

The Convex memory write mutation pins the action and ring, consumes a delegation-manifest use, issues a one-shot grant, checks intent/token authorization, writes a receipt binding manifest and memory data, then inserts the row in one transaction. A conflicting concurrent use sequence refuses rather than spending twice.

No normal in-place value-update API appeared in the inspected local memory module or Convex write path. Convex write inserts a row; local exposes remember and forget. Higher-level correction behavior in uninspected callers is unknown.

Local forget clears plaintext and tombstones the row while retaining its content hash and chain link, then records a forget receipt. Convex erase uses an owner-root signature and leaves a scrubbed countable stub with original hashes plus an erasure receipt. The source warns that database versions/pages may remain during backend retention or until vacuum, and unsalted commitments may permit guessed-value confirmation.

Local recall filters active remember entries by the selected/default chain key, sorts by sequence, and applies an optional tail limit; malformed store content is surfaced as corrupt rather than read as empty. Convex point recall verifies row content against its hash and receipt before returning it to an owner-root or still-authorized delegated writer.

The Convex full-text and vector search implementations return keys only, with content served through the integrity-checking point-read path. Their source comments explicitly say they are benchmark candidates not called by any lane at this revision, so they are not the active recall route.

The local store defaults to chainKey auma-ide and filters reads on the supplied/default key; the inspected local API does not authenticate a caller principal, so the chain key is a namespace filter, not identity proof. Convex writes bind to a manifest owner root; point recall permits that root or its delegated writer while the manifest remains valid, while search is owner-root-only. Convex functions are internal-only and the subproject README describes a self-hosted admin-key boundary.

Local receipts bind actor, chain key, sequence, operation, content hash, previous hash, timestamp and gate-argument hash. verifyChain recomputes links and cross-checks a separate receipt log; code documents that this is not a signature and does not detect an attacker who consistently rewrites both local files. Convex receipts bind manifest, root, subject, fingerprint, use sequence and memory hash; row reads re-derive the content binding. Receipts substantiate recorded fields, not the truth of remembered content.

Source-visible efficiency: the local path parses the stored file and sorts chain entries for recall, and rewrites the full entry file on mutation while appending receipts. Convex uses indexed owner/key reads and bounded candidate pools for search. Verification exposes lengths, counts, flags and failure reasons. These code paths do not provide measured latency, throughput, token, cost or storage results.

metrics.evidence: The code exposes advisory recall and point-read checks, but no answerable or unanswerable probe was run.
No in-place update API appeared in inspected files; no correction workload or stale-value probe was run.
Source describes content scrubbing and residual backend retention; no post-erasure leakage probes were run.
Local chain-key filtering and Convex owner/delegation checks are visible in source, but no cross-scope probes were run.
Receipt and content-hash bindings are source-visible; no response claims were adjudicated against evidence.
Full-file local reads and indexed Convex lookups are implementation observations only; no timed retrievals were collected.
Write and retrieval paths were inspected but no ordered write-then-recall timing probes were run.
No model-token or service-cost measurements were collected for this review.
The repository structure and persistence paths are visible, but stored bytes per item and physical erasure were not measured.

limits.text: This review covers selected source pages at the verified head; it is not a full review of the wider organism, all consumers, deployment configuration, or cryptographic implementation. The repository describes itself as PROVEN-LAB/research engineering rather than a production system.

The local chain has no signed head in the inspected memory module; its receipt cross-check is limited to the two local files it reads. The Convex erasure path leaves commitments and receipt evidence and documents backend-version/page-retention limits. Neither source review establishes end-to-end physical erasure.

Boot recall source says it has no real importer at this revision, with only the pure region transform imported/tested according to its comments. The search/vector functions are described as uncalled candidates. Current deployment and consumer wiring remain unknown because this review did not run the application.

All metric domains remain unmeasured. Source topology and upstream descriptions do not establish answer quality, correction quality, isolation under deployment, deletion completeness, or runtime performance.

benchmark.text: Benchmark not run. No Aukora runtime, tests or benchmark workload were executed. Project metric definitions, fixture and the not_run execution-status record define a separate protocol and are not Aukora results.
